tei:titleStmt.tei:title: יום טוב של ק״ק קארפינטראס לט״ו בחדש כסליו
Poetic Additions for 15 Kislev, for when a heavily armed group of gentiles didn't commit mass slaughter in Carpentras (1512)

tei:div.tei:head: Poetic Additions for 15 Kislev, for when a heavily armed group of gentiles didn't commit mass slaughter in Carpentras (1512)

tei:l.tei:note: At night, before Barkhu, say the following piyyuṭ.
And if it falls on Saturday night, add first:

tei:lg.tei:l: Peoples thank you, God;
all peoples thank you.
Land gives its crop;
God our God will bless us.
God will bless us,
and all the earth’s ends will see Them. (Psalms 67:6–8)
They asked me when my thoughts were wandering,
Where is the Deity’s right hand? (×3)
And where is the arm of the Cause?
Where is Their splendor, Their glory, Their proud hand’s strength?
Could it be withdrawn... (×3)
the hand of the Cause?
From redeeming the people in darkness, awaiting
salvation’s light... (×3)
and known will be the hand of the Cause.
Every day, as long as you remain,
sanctify the Deity, (×3)
and bless the Cause!

tei:l.tei:note: And say the evening prayer as on a regular weekday, up until “Forever we have hoped in You” and say:

tei:lg.tei:l: For the miracles which You showed us,
the congregation of the Hebrews...
You are the wonder-working Deity; (Psalms 77:15)
You have had salvations for us!
On the fifteenth day of the month of Kislev,
As gentile squadsmen rose against us, entered our gates;
bulwarks and mounds they spread to annihilate us,
And to cut off the memory of our remnant,
these worthess ones terrified and discomfited us.
And the cry of the tender children was great and bitter,
for their souls were made aware of death,
nd the women’s pulse was quickening,
as they raised a lament among themselves.
If not for the Master, Cause of Multitudes,
arisen from Their holy habitation, gracing us,
to raise our lean-to, saving,
and removing them from our borders,
But a small remnant left for us! (Isaiah 1:9)
In just a ṡėċȯṅḋ, ȧṅ exit, and they were no more;
they and their wealth was lost.
The Cause loves the gates of Ẓion,
for there Their strength is concealed.
They were for us a fiery wall;
we were not bereft of Their redemption.
For You are our Sovereign and our Redeemer,
who graces and supervises our limited tongues,
to plead Your substantive and noble strength.
And to us silence is praise!
We, Your servants of the diaspora.
Not for our righteousness or our lacking deeds
did You look down from Your holy abode to enliven us,
but rather by merit of the mighty ones of old,
whose hearts were as proper as the entrance to the vestibule.
And due to our wicked deeds
we cannot bring thanksgiving-offerings
for communal wonders.
Thus those You redeemed came
to visit Your Palace in cheering voice,
let our hands be faithful!
And we set this day as rejoicing and festivity
to give laudation and much praise
to Your glory on high.

tei:l.tei:note: And for all that...
And so too say in the grace after meals, in the blessing of the land, before “For everything.”
And say the full Qaddish and Barkhu and ‘Aleinu l’Shabeaḥ.
And in Shaḥarit, say Zmirot as on a regular weekday up until “And in Your Torah it is written, saying...” and after that, say:

tei:lg.tei:l: Reshut

tei:l.tei:note: to the tune of “Y’sod haKol”

tei:lg.tei:l: The Living God in whose hand is all
Reveals Their enigmas, mysteries, and secrets.
Their mighty right hand is visible to Their servant.
They hurry their salvation
and answer in their stress
in the height of Their strength and majesty.
Muḥarrak

tei:l.tei:note: to the tune of “M’tsiv Adama”

tei:lg.tei:l: Go out, my soul, to the living God, constant mighty acts.
For the miracles and for the mighty acts!
I prepare my song to the Dweller in my abodes.
My stressors trembled, my accounters feared.
The Cause’s kindnesses occurred before me
And found in my eyes help in stresses.
In stress, They raised my foot in openness.
I will constantly give praise to my Deity.
They destroyed the foe, in Their kindness, not for my sake
doing wonders uncountable.
Go out, my soul, to the living God, constant mighty acts.

tei:l.tei:note: From “the soul of all life” to “to You alone we thank.”

tei:lg.tei:l: The soul of Your children You brought from groaning to rest
will tell Your wonders,
the time you saved them from stress and it was relief.
You overturned my mourning,
removed my sackcloth and girt me with joy. (Psalms 30:12)
The soul of the awesome one given to slaughter by the stressors
will pray to the Cause,
and will weep, weep, saying “Save me, Cause,
for Your hand is not insufficient!
Give us help from stress! (Psalms 60:13)
The soul of the believers will praise You
for the many wonders You made them,
Awesome in Praises,
acknowledging that in Your kindness rather than their righteousness
did Your right hand and the light of Your face desire them. (Psalms 44:4)
The soul of these days,
them and their race established and accepted upon them
to remember the days of their saving,
and their memory never ceasing from their seed. (Esther 9:28)
The soul of those called by Jacob’s name
call to the Wonder-Worker
in a voice of cheer and thanksgiving,
praising the Deity who reveals hidden things,
saying “Were our mouths full...”

tei:l.tei:note: And finish the prayer as on a regular weekday, but saying “For the miracles” in the thanksgiving blessing.
After the standing prayer, say a full hallel without a blessing.

tei:lg.tei:l: A poem for Hallel:
Send Your rescue to the exiled people,
bring down a wonder into the prison-pit!
In place of its sacrifice, to You ascends a psalm-song,
to fully recite the great hallel.

tei:l.tei:note: Before taking out the Torah:

tei:lg.tei:l: Thank the Cause who is good,
for eternal is Their kindness!
Let the Cause’s redeemed say
that They redeemed them from the stressor’s hand.
And from the lands gathered them,
from East and West, North and South.
They wandered in the wild,
in the wasteland-way,
finding no habitable town.
Hungry and thirsty too,
in them their soul was weary.
And they cried in their stress to the Cause,
who saved them from their straits.
They led them straightaway,
to go to a habitable town.
Let them thank the Cause for Their kindness
and Their wonders to human beings!

tei:l.tei:note: And take out the Torah scroll
and three people read from Parashat B’shallaḥ:
Kohen (first ‘aliyah): Exodus 14:15—25
Levi (second ‘aliyah): Exodus 14:26—31
Yisrael (third ‘aliyah): Exodus 15:1–26 ​
And return the Torah scroll to its place,
and finish the prayer as on any other weekday on which petitionary prayers are not said.

tei:note.tei:p: In the Modim prayer, the final passage before an Al haNissim addition is inserted.
The original Hebrew printing says בְּנֵיהֶם “their children” in place of “among themselves.” This is a worse rhyme, and makes no sense in context, so it was emended.
Zechariah 2:17

The word רֶָׄגַׄעׄ is marked with upper dots, because the events in question occurred in the year 5273 (24 November 1512 Julian) and the gematria of רֶָׄגַׄעׄ is 273, the short count for the year. This is reflected in the English with upper dots on “ṡėċȯṅḋ ȧṅ” which has the sum of 100+5+3+60+50+4+1+50=273 in English gematria.

An introduction. In this case, to the cycle of piyyutim inserted into the Nishmat prayer. This is a piyyuṭ also found in some manuscripts of the Catalan rite (although not in the Siddur Katalunya), recited as a reshut on Purim.

A piyyut introducing the Nishmat prayer, the first (after the reshut) in the cycle of Nishmat additions. This is a piyyuṭ also found in some manuscripts of the Catalan rite (although not in the Siddur Katalunya), recited as a muḥarrak on Shavu’ot or Simḥat Torah. Interestingly enough, the term “Great Hallel” usually refers to Psalms 136 rather than the festival Hallel of Psalms 113-118 intended here. In this case “great” must be interpreted as an adjectival modifier rather than part of the title. In the siddur, the hallel is not printed here, but a note is included reading “The full Hallel is written in the new moon section.”
